title: Mass as pairing: an explicit Majorana mass on half of a generation does not seesaw in symmetric mass generation
comment: 21 pages, 4 figures, 17 tables; code and machine-checked claims at https://github.com/PiotrTopa/mass-as-pairing (v1.0.1, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23178329), data DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23117210
summary: A fermion mass pairs a field with a partner of conjugate charge: elementary (Higgs-Dirac), self-conjugate (seesaw) or a three-fermion composite (symmetric mass generation, SMG). We give half of a Spin(10)-like generation an explicit Majorana mass in a four-dimensional SMG model and ask what the other half does in a phase with no condensate. With the source on, every mass-type term of the unsourced half averages to zero under the symmetry group of the sourced action, so a light mass term, and a seesaw's light-heavy mixing, requires a spontaneously broken symmetry; exact on the lattice and a general proposition. The source is colour-democratic (a Delta_R-type mass on every flavour's right-handed taste doublet); the single-nu_R split lies outside the positivity class used but inside the symmetry statement. Measured up to 8^4: (i) in the symmetric-gap phase, with the source screened to at most 1.1% of free, the unsourced half's single-fermion readout stays at 0.3% of free while its pair susceptibility rises from 0.2% to 1.2-1.7% at h=2; on like mode sets it falls with the volume, on (4^4,8^4) no inequivalent light mass channel grows faster than free, and symmetry breaking is not resolved at L<=8; (ii) at the critical point the explicit mass collapses the critical sigma channel and moves the light half toward free as a saturating crossover, not a power law; direction tests (MIXED by their pre-registered letter) are consistent with a critical coupling rising with the mass; y_c(h) is not located. Pole versus zero of the light propagator at p->0 is not measured. The outcomes are readings after pre-registered tests that mostly returned no verdict. Also: no first-order signature of the merged transition at L<=8, a Z_4-odd response handed to a lattice composite, and flavour democracy of the positivity class. Every claim has an evidence class and a runnable check.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the behavior of fermion masses in a four-dimensional symmetric mass generation (SMG) model, focusing on the implications of an explicit Majorana mass for half of a Spin(10)-like generation. The study examines the light mass term and seesaw mechanism's light-heavy mixing, which requires a spontaneously broken symmetry. It also discusses the impact of a color-democratic source on the system, and provides numerical evidence up to 8^4 lattice sizes without finding clear indications of spontaneous symmetry breaking or first-order phase transitions.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to understand how giving half of a Spin(10)-like generation an explicit Majorana mass affects the other half in the absence of a condensate, and under what conditions a light mass term and a seesaw mechanism can occur within the context of a four-dimensional SMG model.
AI.method: The method involves theoretical analysis and numerical simulations on lattices up to 8^4. The researchers use a color-democratic source and investigate the single-fermion readout and pair susceptibility of the unsourced half, as well as the critical point behavior and the light propagator's pole versus zero at p->0.
AI.result: In the symmetric-gap phase, with the source screened, the unsourced half's single-fermion readout remains low, while the pair susceptibility increases. No inequivalent light mass channel grows faster than free, and no spontaneous symmetry breaking is observed at lattice sizes L<=8. At the critical point, the explicit mass collapses the critical sigma channel, and the light half moves toward the free state as a saturating crossover rather than a power law. No first-order signature of a merged transition is found, and there is a flavor democracy of the positivity class.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that the presence of an explicit Majorana mass for half of a Spin(10)-like generation does not lead to spontaneous symmetry breaking or a first-order phase transition for the studied lattice sizes. The findings suggest that a light mass term and seesaw mechanism require a spontaneously broken symmetry, and the light fermions' behavior is consistent with a saturating crossover at the critical point.
